Part one, introduction to Bangladesh.
Bangladesh is a country in South Asia
and it is bordered by India to the West,
North and East and Myanmar to the Southeast.
It is also very close to the Bay of Bengal to the South.
The capital city of Bangladesh is Dhaka
and it is the largest city in the country.
Dhaka is a very busy and crowded city
with tall buildings, busy streets, markets and many people.
There are around 170 million people living in Bangladesh,
making it one of the most densely populated countries
in the world.
The official language of Bangladesh is Bengali
but many people also speak English.
English is used a lot in business, education and government.
People in Bangladesh are known for their hospitality
and they are always ready to welcome guests
with a smile and good food.
Part two, geography and climate.
Bangladesh is a flat country with many rivers.
The largest river is the Padma River
and there are also many other big rivers
like the Jamuna and the Meghna.
These rivers are very important to the people of Bangladesh
because they help with farming and transportation.
The country is also known for its beautiful countryside
and Greenland scapes
because Bangladesh is close to the Bay of Bengal,
it has a tropical climate.

Bangladesh is also home to the Sundar Bands,

It is famous for being the home of the Bengal tiger

Part three, food in Bangladesh.
Bangladeshi food is very delicious
and often includes rice, lentils, vegetables and spices.
The food is very flavorful and has many different tastes.
Some of the most popular dishes in Bangladesh include biryani,
a special rice dish with meat, spices and vegetables.
It is very popular in Dhaka and other big cities.
Shorsha illish, a dish made with hillsafish,
cooked in mustard sauce.
It is a national dish and very loved
by the people of Bangladesh.
Dal, lentil soup.
It is usually served with rice
and eaten every day by many people in Bangladesh.
Pita, traditional sweet cakes made from rice flour
and filled with coconut or jaggery.
These are often made during special holidays and festivals.
People in Bangladesh also love drinking tea,
especially cha, which is milk tea with sugar and spices.
It is common to have tea in the morning or afternoon,
often with snacks.
Part four, culture and traditions.
Bangladesh has a rich culture
with a mix of traditional and modern influences.
The people of Bangladesh love to celebrate
and they have many festivals and traditions
that are very important to them.
One of the most important celebrations in Bangladesh
is Pohalo Boyshak, which is the Bengali New Year.
It is celebrated with parades, music, dances
and traditional food.
On this day, people wear new clothes
and everyone celebrates the start of a new year
according to the Bengali calendar.
Another famous tradition in Bangladesh is ball music,
which is folk music played with traditional instruments
like the Dottara and Ekdara.
The songs are very emotional
and often express love, life and spirituality.
Bangladeshis are also famous for their hospitality.
When visitors come to a Bangladeshi home,
it is common to be offered tea, sweets
and sometimes a full meal,
as it is considered a sign of respect and kindness.
Part five, sports and activities.
People in Bangladesh love sports
and the most popular sport is cricket.
Bangladesh has a strong national cricket team
and many people watch cricket matches on TV
or go to the stadium to see the games.
Football, also called soccer, is also popular,
especially in the villages.
In addition to these,
there are also other activities people enjoy.
Basketball.
Many young people play basketball in schools and in parks.
Water sports.
Bangladesh has many rivers and beaches,
so activities like boating, sailing
and swimming are very common.
Cycling.
Cycling is a popular activity in both cities and villages,
as it is an easy and cheap way to travel.
Part six, famous places to visit.
